etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: Adapted borrowing (1640s; 1582 as deletorious) of New Latin dēlētērius, dēlētōrius +‎ -ous, from Ancient Greek δηλητήριος (dēlētḗrios, “noxious, deleterious”), from δηλητήρ (dēlētḗr, “a destroyer”), from δηλέομαι (dēléomai, “I hurt, damage, spoil, waste”). Not related to delete or deleble. Doublet of deletery.
senses: (formal) Harmful, often in a subtle or unexpected way.
